dashboard.label: ITSI Setup
dashboard.description: How to install IT Service Intelligence (premium) from your .spl file — and why it's manual.

html.p: ITSI is a premium, separately-licensed Splunk app — it isn't part of the config-as-code build (licensing + size), so it's installed by hand from the .spl file you have. This page is the repeatable checklist.

Heads-up: ITSI is heavy (its own indexes, KV store, saved searches, ML deps) and needs a run-time license (trial or purchased). On this reset-each-session VM you'll re-do this after every reset. For a lighter demo of the same idea, use the interim "Service Health" dashboard instead.

search.query: | rest /services/apps/local | search title=itsi OR title=SA-ITOA OR label="*Service Intelligence*" | eval Status="installed" | table title label version Status

html.h3: Why the Web UI upload fails on this box
html.p: The browser upload cannot work here. In Splunk 10.0+ there is a 512 MB limit hard-coded into the Web UI component itself. It is not the max_upload_size setting — raising that (we set it to 1 GB in apply.sh) does not lift the UI cap. ITSI is well over 512 MB, so "Package is too large, must be less than 500 MB" is expected and unavoidable through the browser on 10.x. Install it server-side instead (both options below have no size limit).
html.h3: Install it (pick one — both are server-side, no size limit)

p.b: A) Auto-fetch at boot from a URL (no file-moving) — recommended:

html.p: Host your ITSI .spl anywhere the lab can reach (your file host, a temporary signed link, an internal server), then run apply.sh — it prompts for Direct URL(s) of .spl/.tgz apps (or set SPLUNK_INSTALL_URLS). It curls the package and extracts it into etc/apps before Splunk starts. Nothing is committed to the repo, and it re-installs automatically on every session reset.

p.b: B) CLI, if the .spl is already on the box:

html.pre: sudo -u splunk /opt/splunk/bin/splunk install app /tmp/itsi.spl -auth admin:C1sco12345 sudo systemctl restart Splunkd
html.p: The CLI install app command has no upload cap — the 512 MB limit is a Web-UI-only restriction.

ol.li: License: ITSI needs its own license. Add a trial/eval under Settings ▸ Licensing if prompted, or ITSI runs in a limited/trial state.
First run: open the IT Service Intelligence app — it completes a one-time setup and creates its indexes (e.g. itsi_summary) + KV store.
Point it at lab data: create a couple of Services (e.g. "London Hosts", "Berlin Hosts") with KPIs from our metrics/syslog (index=*_metrics, index=*_linux) to get glass tables and health scores.

html.p: RBAC note: ITSI has its own role model; the lab's location roles won't automatically map to ITSI service access.

html.h3: Making it survive the session reset
html.p: The VM wipes each session, so a manual install is lost. Both boot options below re-install automatically on every reset — no file-moving:

ul.li: URL auto-fetch (any account) — set SPLUNK_INSTALL_URLS="https://your-host/itsi.spl" (or answer the prompt) when running apply.sh. Works regardless of Splunkbase entitlement; it still needs an ITSI run-time license after install.

Splunkbase auto-download — if your splunk.com account is entitled to ITSI, add its Splunkbase app id to the boot install: SPLUNKBASE_APP_IDS="7931 <itsi_id>" when running apply.sh (same flow as the MCP Server). First download of any Splunkbase app needs its license terms accepted once in a browser at splunkbase.splunk.com while logged in, or the API returns HTTP 403.

html.p: Version check: make sure your ITSI build supports Splunk 10.4 — if the app won't load after restart, that's the usual cause.
